[spaceBasedObservation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/astronomicalInstrumentsAndEvidence/telescopesAndDetectors/skills/spaceBasedObservation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare observations above and below Earth's atmosphere in terms of accessible wavelengths and atmospheric interference.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare observations from space with those made through Earth's atmosphere.

### Celestial Mechanics

Groups: 3 · Skills: 15

[celestialMechanics.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/celestialMechanics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** This domain concerns how gravity and angular momentum govern orbital motion, rotation and mutual perturbations across planetary and stellar systems. Geometrical appearances arising from these motions are addressed separately when the observational phenomenon itself is the competency.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how gravity and motion shape the paths and rotations of objects in space.

#### Dynamical Interactions

Skills: 4

[dynamicalInteractions.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/dynamicalInteractions/dynamicalInteractions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Real celestial systems include many bodies, so resonances, tides and perturbations can alter otherwise idealized orbital motion.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how tides and other gravitational interactions alter celestial motions.

##### Gravitational Perturbations

[gravitationalPerturbations.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/dynamicalInteractions/skills/gravitationalPerturbations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret departures from a simple two-body orbit caused by additional gravitational influences.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how extra gravitational forces change an otherwise simple orbit.

##### Orbital Resonances

[orbitalResonances.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/dynamicalInteractions/skills/orbitalResonances.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize recurring period relationships that can organize or destabilize orbital systems.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when repeating orbital timing relationships affect a system.

##### Orbital Stability

[orbitalStability.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/dynamicalInteractions/skills/orbitalStability.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate how changing orbital parameters and interactions can affect whether a system remains dynamically stable.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore what helps an orbital system remain stable—or makes it change.

##### Tidal Forces

[tidalForces.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/dynamicalInteractions/skills/tidalForces.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain differences in gravitational pull across an extended body and their consequences for distortion and orbital evolution.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how unequal gravitational pulls across a world create tides.

#### Gravitational Motion

Skills: 6

[gravitationalMotion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/gravitationalMotion/gravitationalMotion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Gravitational interactions produce trajectories governed by mass, initial conditions and the reference frame in which motion is described.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how gravity governs the motion of celestial bodies.

##### Barycentric Motion

[barycentricMotion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/gravitationalMotion/skills/barycentricMotion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why interacting celestial bodies orbit a shared center of mass rather than one body always remaining stationary.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why two orbiting bodies move around a shared centre of mass.

##### Kepler's First Law

[keplersFirstLaw.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/gravitationalMotion/skills/keplersFirstLaw.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Apply the elliptical-orbit relation, with the central gravitating body at one focus in the idealized two-body model, to the geometry of bound orbits.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how an ideal orbit can follow an ellipse with the central body at one focus.

##### Kepler's Second Law

[keplersSecondLaw.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/gravitationalMotion/skills/keplersSecondLaw.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use the equal-areas-in-equal-times relation to explain variation in orbital speed as an orbiting body changes its distance from the central focus.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why an orbiting body moves faster when it is closer to the central body.

##### Kepler's Third Law

[keplersThirdLaw.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/gravitationalMotion/skills/keplersThirdLaw.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate the square of orbital period to the cube of semi-major axis with the appropriate gravitational mass dependence and limitations of the two-body model.

**User-friendly description (en):** Relate an object's orbital period to the size of its orbit and the gravitating mass.

##### Orbital Energy

[orbitalEnergy.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/gravitationalMotion/skills/orbitalEnergy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate gravitational potential and kinetic energy to bound and unbound orbital trajectories.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how energy determines whether an orbit remains bound or escapes.

##### Universal Gravitation

[universalGravitation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/gravitationalMotion/skills/universalGravitation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Apply the dependence of gravitational attraction on interacting masses and separation to astronomical situations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use the masses and distances of objects to reason about gravitational attraction.

#### Orbits and Rotations

Skills: 5

[orbitsAndRotations.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/orbitsAndRotations/orbitsAndRotations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Orbital shapes and body orientations are specified through distinct physical parameters that affect long-term celestial behavior.

**User-friendly description (en):** Describe and compare the shapes, periods and orientations of celestial motions.

##### Axial Rotation

[axialRotation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/orbitsAndRotations/skills/axialRotation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe the spin of a world about its axis, including rotation period and direction, independently of the tilt or precession of that axis.

**User-friendly description (en):** Describe a celestial body's rotation about its own axis.

##### Axial Tilt

[axialTilt.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/orbitsAndRotations/skills/axialTilt.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret the angle between a body's spin axis and orbital reference direction and explain its influence on illumination geometry and seasons.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how the tilt of a world's axis changes the pattern of illumination.

##### Orbital Elements

[orbitalElements.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/orbitsAndRotations/skills/orbitalElements.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret inclination, eccentricity and other orbital descriptors when comparing celestial trajectories.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read the parameters that describe an orbit's shape and orientation.

##### Orbital Periods

[orbitalPeriods.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/orbitsAndRotations/skills/orbitalPeriods.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret the time needed to complete an orbit and compare sidereal and synodic periods, distinguishing orbital revolution from rotation about the body's own axis.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish the time taken to orbit another body from the time taken to spin.

##### Synchronous Rotation

[synchronousRotation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/celestialMechanics/orbitsAndRotations/skills/synchronousRotation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how spin–orbit coupling can produce a repeating orientation toward an orbital partner.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why some worlds keep nearly the same face toward their orbital partners.

### Cosmic Objects

Groups: 2 · Skills: 7

[cosmicObjects.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/cosmicObjects.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** An overview of what kinds of physical objects and extended structures exist beyond Earth and how they are identified and organized. It teaches classification across cosmic scales and distinguishes an object's physical nature from its environment or apparent visual form; detailed physics belongs to the specialized planetary, stellar, galactic and cosmological domains.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the different kinds of objects and structures found in the universe and how astronomers classify them.

#### Object Families

Skills: 4

[objectFamilies.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/objectFamilies/objectFamilies.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Classification of astronomical entities requires more than their appearance in a photograph: a point source, a diffuse cloud, a cluster and an extended galaxy may be distinguished by physical evidence and scale.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how astronomers identify different types of objects using physical evidence rather than appearance alone.

##### Celestial Object Classification

[celestialObjectClassification.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/objectFamilies/skills/celestialObjectClassification.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Classify astronomical sources as stellar bodies, planetary bodies, compact remnants, diffuse clouds, star clusters, galaxies or other broad physical types using characteristic evidence rather than appearance alone.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize major categories of celestial objects by their physical properties.

##### Diffuse and Composite Objects

[diffuseAndCompositeObjects.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/objectFamilies/skills/diffuseAndCompositeObjects.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Differentiate diffuse nebulae, gravitationally associated groups and composite galaxies by their constituents, structure and binding rather than surface resemblance.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish gas clouds, star groups and galaxies by what they contain and how they are organized.

##### Objects and Phenomena

[objectsAndPhenomena.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/objectFamilies/skills/objectsAndPhenomena.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish enduring physical objects and systems from observed events or effects such as eclipses, meteors, flares and transient brightenings, even when both occur in object catalogs.

**User-friendly description (en):** Tell the difference between a lasting celestial object and an event such as an eclipse or flare.

##### Stellar, Substellar and Planetary Boundaries

[stellarSubstellarAndPlanetaryBoundaries.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/objectFamilies/skills/stellarSubstellarAndPlanetaryBoundaries.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare physically distinct stars, brown dwarfs and planetary-mass bodies using fusion and mass constraints while acknowledging uncertainties near classification boundaries.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how stars, brown dwarfs and planets differ, including where their categories overlap.

#### Organization and Membership

Skills: 3

[organizationAndMembership.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/organizationAndMembership/organizationAndMembership.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A body's membership in a system is a different property from its type; the same class of object can be gravitationally bound, ejected or found in a sparse galactic environment.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how objects belong to larger astronomical systems or travel independently.

##### Free-Floating Planets

[freeFloatingPlanets.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/organizationAndMembership/skills/freeFloatingPlanets.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain planetary-mass objects not gravitationally bound to a host star, including proposed ejection or isolated-formation origins and detection by microlensing or thermal infrared emission; distinguish low illumination from a complete absence of radiation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how planets without a host star may form, move and be detected.

##### Gravitationally Bound Systems

[gravitationallyBoundSystems.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/organizationAndMembership/skills/gravitationallyBoundSystems.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish satellite systems, planetary systems, multiple stars, star clusters, galaxies and galaxy clusters by physical membership and characteristic scales.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare planetary systems, star clusters, galaxies and other gravitationally connected systems.

##### Object Membership and Isolation

[objectMembershipAndIsolation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmicObjects/organizationAndMembership/skills/objectMembershipAndIsolation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine whether an astronomical object is a member of a larger bound system or is apparently isolated, and explain why gravitational context does not by itself determine intrinsic object type.

**User-friendly description (en):** Find out whether an object belongs to a larger system without confusing that with what kind of object it is.

### Cosmology

Groups: 5 · Skills: 17

[cosmology.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmology.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Cosmology tests models for the Universe's large-scale composition, history and expansion using observations with known horizons and uncertainties. Unresolved questions must remain distinguishable from established evidence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Investigate the Universe's expansion, history and large-scale structure using astronomical evidence.

#### Cosmic Components and Constraints

Skills: 3

[cosmicComponentsAndConstraints.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicComponentsAndConstraints/cosmicComponentsAndConstraints.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Gravitational and expansion measurements constrain otherwise unseen components, while cosmological parameters and theoretical uncertainties limit the interpretations that can be supported by available evidence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how cosmic measurements point to components and questions we cannot yet fully explain.

##### Dark Energy Evidence

[darkEnergyEvidence.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicComponentsAndConstraints/skills/darkEnergyEvidence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why observations of accelerated expansion motivate a dark-energy component or changes to gravitational models.

**User-friendly description (en):** Examine the evidence that cosmic expansion is accelerating.

##### Dark Matter Evidence

[darkMatterEvidence.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicComponentsAndConstraints/skills/darkMatterEvidence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret dynamical, lensing and cosmological evidence for unseen gravitating mass while recognizing remaining theoretical alternatives.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why astronomers infer unseen matter from gravitational evidence.

##### Limits of Cosmological Knowledge

[limitsOfCosmologicalKnowledge.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicComponentsAndConstraints/skills/limitsOfCosmologicalKnowledge.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish empirical constraints from open problems concerning early conditions, dark components and the global extent of the Universe.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish what observations establish about the Universe from major unanswered questions.

#### Cosmic Expansion

Skills: 4

[cosmicExpansion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicExpansion/cosmicExpansion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Large-scale redshift patterns support an evolving cosmic geometry, not an ordinary explosion into pre-existing empty space.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn what observations reveal about the expansion of the Universe.

##### Cosmological Models

[cosmologicalModels.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicExpansion/skills/cosmologicalModels.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare the predictions and assumptions of simplified expanding-Universe models against observations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare models of cosmic expansion with their assumptions and predictions.

##### Cosmological Redshift

[cosmologicalRedshift.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicExpansion/skills/cosmologicalRedshift.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain wavelength stretching associated with the expansion of space, distinguishing it from local Doppler motion.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how expanding space stretches the wavelengths of travelling light.

##### Expansion Versus Bound Systems

[expansionVersusBoundSystems.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicExpansion/skills/expansionVersusBoundSystems.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why the expansion of the Universe does not automatically enlarge gravitationally bound local systems.

**User-friendly description (en):** See why expanding space does not simply stretch planets, stars or galaxies apart.

##### Hubble–Lemaître Relation

[hubbleLemaitreRelation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicExpansion/skills/hubbleLemaitreRelation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate galaxy recession measurements and distance to empirical evidence for expansion within its domain of applicability.

**User-friendly description (en):** Relate measured galaxy distances and redshifts to evidence for cosmic expansion.

#### Cosmic Scales

Skills: 4

[cosmicScales.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicScales/cosmicScales.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distances and times become linked by the finite speed of light, which limits how much of the Universe can be observed.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the immense distances and times involved in observing the cosmos.

##### Cosmic Distance Measures

[cosmicDistanceMeasures.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicScales/skills/cosmicDistanceMeasures.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish common cosmological distance concepts when relating observed brightness, redshift and scale.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare the different ways cosmologists define and measure distance.

##### Cosmic Horizons

[cosmicHorizons.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicScales/skills/cosmicHorizons.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret limits on observable or causally connected regions without treating them as physical walls.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore limits on how far signals can reach us or influence other regions.

##### Lookback Time

[lookbackTime.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicScales/skills/lookbackTime.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why distant observations show objects at earlier cosmic epochs.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover why looking farther into space also means looking into the past.

##### Observable Universe

[observableUniverse.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicScales/skills/observableUniverse.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish the observable region set by signal travel and cosmic history from claims about the entire Universe.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why the observable Universe is not necessarily the whole Universe.

#### Cosmic Structure and Evolution

Skills: 2

[cosmicStructureAndEvolution.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicStructureAndEvolution/cosmicStructureAndEvolution.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Density perturbations, gravity and cosmic expansion shape the cosmic web over time. This branch focuses on spatial organization and dynamical evolution, as distinct from the initial hot state or the physical nature of the Universe's dark components.

**User-friendly description (en):** Investigate how gravity shapes matter into large structures over cosmic history.

##### Cosmic Structure Formation

[cosmicStructureFormation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicStructureAndEvolution/skills/cosmicStructureFormation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how initially small matter-density differences grow into galaxies and large-scale structure.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how tiny early differences in matter density developed into cosmic structure.

##### Cosmic Web

[cosmicWeb.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/cosmicStructureAndEvolution/skills/cosmicWeb.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe how filaments, clusters and voids trace the large-scale distribution of matter.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the vast network of galactic filaments, clusters and empty regions.

#### Early-Universe Models and Evidence

Skills: 4

[earlyUniverseModelsAndEvidence.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/earlyUniverseModelsAndEvidence/earlyUniverseModelsAndEvidence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The early hot and dense Universe is reconstructed from relic radiation, primordial abundances and theoretical models whose predictions and evidence have different degrees of support.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the evidence used to reconstruct the early, hot Universe.

##### Cosmic Inflation

[cosmicInflation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/earlyUniverseModelsAndEvidence/skills/cosmicInflation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the hypothesized early accelerated-expansion phase, distinguish its predicted consequences from direct observation and evaluate what existing cosmic evidence can and cannot establish.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the idea of cosmic inflation and distinguish predictions from confirmed evidence.

##### Cosmic Microwave Background

[cosmicMicrowaveBackground.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/earlyUniverseModelsAndEvidence/skills/cosmicMicrowaveBackground.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret relic microwave radiation and its spatial variations as evidence about the early Universe.

**User-friendly description (en):** Investigate the faint microwave glow left from the early Universe.

##### Hot Big Bang Model

[hotBigBangModel.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/earlyUniverseModelsAndEvidence/skills/hotBigBangModel.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the evidence-supported early evolution of the observable Universe without claiming that the model fully explains its ultimate origin.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover what the hot Big Bang model explains—and what it does not establish.

##### Primordial Nucleosynthesis

[primordialNucleosynthesis.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/cosmology/earlyUniverseModelsAndEvidence/skills/primordialNucleosynthesis.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the predicted formation of light nuclei and why their observed abundances test early-Universe models.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how early-universe models predict the amounts of light elements.

### Earth, Moon and Sun

Groups: 4 · Skills: 14

[earthMoonAndSun.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/earthMoonAndSun.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Here the distinctive geometry of Earth's viewpoint, rotation and revolution produces observable cycles. The scientific emphasis is on explaining familiar sky events from physical arrangements rather than on general geography or atmospheric meteorology.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how the movements and positions of Earth, the Moon and the Sun create familiar patterns in the sky.

#### Earth–Moon Interactions

Skills: 3

[earthMoonInteractions.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/earthMoonInteractions/earthMoonInteractions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The Earth–Moon system is a long-term dynamical pair whose interactions create measurable effects on Earth and its satellite.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how the Moon and Earth influence each other through gravity.

##### Lunar Orbit and Month

[lunarOrbitAndMonth.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/earthMoonInteractions/skills/lunarOrbitAndMonth.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish the Moon's orbital cycle from the phase cycle by considering Earth's simultaneous revolution around the Sun.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare the Moon's journey around Earth with its repeating cycle of phases.

##### Lunar Tidal Evolution

[lunarTidalEvolution.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/earthMoonInteractions/skills/lunarTidalEvolution.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how tidal dissipation affects Earth's rotation and the Moon's orbital distance over long timescales.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how tidal interactions slowly change Earth's rotation and the Moon's orbit.

##### Ocean Tides

[oceanTides.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/earthMoonInteractions/skills/oceanTides.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the dominant lunar and solar gravitational contributions to periodic changes in sea level, distinguishing ideal equilibrium tides from local coastal conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how the Moon and Sun help produce ocean tides.

#### Eclipses and Alignments

Skills: 3

[eclipsesAndAlignments.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/eclipsesAndAlignments/eclipsesAndAlignments.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Occultation and shadow phenomena depend on an observer's line of sight and the relative positions and apparent sizes of bodies.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how eclipses depend on the alignment of celestial objects and their shadows.

##### Eclipse Seasons

[eclipseSeasons.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/eclipsesAndAlignments/skills/eclipseSeasons.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why solar and lunar eclipses are not observed at every new or full Moon, using orbital inclination and alignment.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover why a new or full Moon does not produce an eclipse every month.

##### Lunar Eclipses

[lunarEclipses.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/eclipsesAndAlignments/skills/lunarEclipses.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the conditions and stages of a lunar eclipse as the Moon encounters Earth's shadow.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how Earth casts its shadow on the Moon during a lunar eclipse.

##### Solar Eclipses

[solarEclipses.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/eclipsesAndAlignments/skills/solarEclipses.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the conditions, shadow regions and different observational appearances of a solar eclipse.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain when a solar eclipse happens and why its appearance varies by location.

#### Lunar Appearance

Skills: 4

[lunarAppearance.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/lunarAppearance/lunarAppearance.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The Moon's changing appearance follows its illumination and orbital viewing geometry, not changes to its intrinsic light production.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how the Moon's movement and sunlight change what we see from Earth.

##### Lunar Libration

[lunarLibration.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/lunarAppearance/skills/lunarLibration.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why changing perspective exposes slightly different portions of the lunar surface over time.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover why slightly different parts of the Moon become visible over time.

##### Lunar Motion

[lunarMotion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/lunarAppearance/skills/lunarMotion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Trace the Moon's changing position against background stars across successive nights.

**User-friendly description (en):** Track how the Moon changes position against the stars from night to night.

##### Lunar Phases

[lunarPhases.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/lunarAppearance/skills/lunarPhases.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the repeating illuminated shapes visible from Earth through the Sun–Moon–observer geometry.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain the changing shape of the sunlit Moon throughout its phases.

##### Near and Far Lunar Hemispheres

[nearAndFarLunarHemispheres.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/lunarAppearance/skills/nearAndFarLunarHemispheres.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish the hemisphere generally facing Earth from the opposite hemisphere without equating the far side with permanent darkness.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why the far side of the Moon is not always dark.

#### Terrestrial Sky Cycles

Skills: 4

[terrestrialSkyCycles.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/terrestrialSkyCycles/terrestrialSkyCycles.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Earth's orientation with respect to sunlight generates daily and annual changes in the visible sky and the duration of daylight.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how Earth's rotation and tilt shape daylight and seasonal changes.

##### Day and Night

[dayAndNight.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/terrestrialSkyCycles/skills/dayAndNight.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the alternation of illumination and darkness through Earth's rotation rather than the Sun physically circling Earth.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why Earth's rotation brings alternating daylight and darkness.

##### Seasons

[seasons.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/terrestrialSkyCycles/skills/seasons.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain seasonal solar illumination using Earth's axial tilt and orbital revolution rather than changes in Earth–Sun distance alone.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how Earth's tilted axis produces the seasons.

##### Solar Altitude and Daylight

[solarAltitudeAndDaylight.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/terrestrialSkyCycles/skills/solarAltitudeAndDaylight.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate the Sun's apparent height and daily path to latitude, date and daylight duration.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how the Sun's apparent height and the length of daylight change with place and season.

##### Solstices and Equinoxes

[solsticesAndEquinoxes.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/earthMoonAndSun/terrestrialSkyCycles/skills/solsticesAndEquinoxes.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain these seasonal reference points from the changing Sun–Earth geometry and the distribution of daylight.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand what makes solstices and equinoxes special points in the year.

### Exoplanetary Systems

Groups: 3 · Skills: 13

[exoplanetarySystems.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetarySystems.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Planetary systems beyond the Sun provide evidence about the diversity of worlds and formation outcomes. Detection, physical inference and habitability are separated to avoid treating an apparent signal as proof of a specific environment.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore planets beyond our Solar System and what their discoveries reveal about other planetary systems.

#### Exoplanet Characterization

Skills: 5

[exoplanetCharacterization.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetCharacterization/exoplanetCharacterization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Planet properties are inferred by combining signals and interpreting assumptions, with important differences between measured quantities and theoretical models.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how researchers infer the properties of exoplanets from indirect observations.

##### Exoplanet Atmospheric Spectra

[exoplanetAtmosphericSpectra.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetCharacterization/skills/exoplanetAtmosphericSpectra.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret transit or emission spectra as evidence about atmospheric constituents and conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how a planet's spectrum provides clues to its atmosphere.

##### Exoplanet Bulk Composition

[exoplanetBulkComposition.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetCharacterization/skills/exoplanetBulkComposition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate a planet's mass-radius behavior to plausible internal materials while recognizing model degeneracy.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use mass and radius to investigate possible planetary materials without assuming one answer.

##### Exoplanet Mass

[exoplanetMass.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetCharacterization/skills/exoplanetMass.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Infer a planet's mass from orbital effects, including limits set by viewing geometry and models.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how a planet's gravitational effects help estimate its mass.

##### Exoplanet Orbital Properties

[exoplanetOrbitalProperties.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetCharacterization/skills/exoplanetOrbitalProperties.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Infer or compare orbital period, eccentricity and star–planet distance using available data.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare the periods, shapes and sizes of exoplanet orbits.

##### Exoplanet Radius

[exoplanetRadius.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetCharacterization/skills/exoplanetRadius.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Infer a planet's size from transit or other observations and explain its dependence on stellar parameters.

**User-friendly description (en):** Estimate a distant planet's size using a transit and information about its star.

#### Exoplanet Detection

Skills: 4

[exoplanetDetection.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetDetection/exoplanetDetection.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Finding planets around distant stars relies on measured effects and each method has a characteristic sensitivity and ambiguity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover the methods astronomers use to find planets around distant stars.

##### Direct Imaging

[directImaging.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetDetection/skills/directImaging.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain when a planet can be resolved separately from its host star and why brightness contrast is challenging.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why photographing a planet beside its bright host star is difficult.

##### Gravitational Microlensing

[gravitationalMicrolensing.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetDetection/skills/gravitationalMicrolensing.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how temporary lensing signatures can reveal otherwise difficult-to-detect planetary companions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how gravity can briefly magnify a distant star's light and reveal a planet.

##### Radial-Velocity Detection

[radialVelocityDetection.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetDetection/skills/radialVelocityDetection.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret periodic stellar spectral shifts as evidence for an orbiting companion and constrain its mass.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use a star's changing spectral motion to infer the pull of an orbiting planet.

##### Transit Detection

[transitDetection.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/exoplanetDetection/skills/transitDetection.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how repeated stellar dimming can indicate a planet crossing a star's disk and why geometry matters.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how a repeating dip in starlight may reveal a planet passing in front of its star.

#### System Diversity

Skills: 4

[systemDiversity.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/systemDiversity/systemDiversity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Comparing observed systems reveals patterns and exceptions relative to Solar System expectations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how planetary systems can differ greatly from our own.

##### Circumstellar Habitable Zones

[circumstellarHabitableZones.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/systemDiversity/skills/circumstellarHabitableZones.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret the range of stellar irradiation permitting surface liquid water under stated atmospheric assumptions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand what a star's habitable zone does—and does not—tell us about liquid water.

##### Exoplanet System Architectures

[exoplanetSystemArchitectures.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/systemDiversity/skills/exoplanetSystemArchitectures.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare tightly packed, resonant, eccentric and other planetary arrangements using orbital evidence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare systems with tightly packed planets, unusual orbits or orbital resonances.

##### Limits of Habitability Indicators

[limitsOfHabitabilityIndicators.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/systemDiversity/skills/limitsOfHabitabilityIndicators.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate why receiving suitable starlight or being Earth-sized does not establish a habitable world.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize why an Earth-sized planet in the right orbit is not automatically habitable.

##### Planetary Migration

[planetaryMigration.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/exoplanetarySystems/systemDiversity/skills/planetaryMigration.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how interactions with disks or other planets can change orbital locations after formation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how planets may move to different orbits after forming.

### Interstellar and Galactic Astronomy

Groups: 4 · Skills: 16

[interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** This domain investigates matter between stars and the structure, dynamics and transformations of galaxies. The Milky Way is one case, while distant galaxies reveal different environments and stages of evolution.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the matter between stars and how galaxies form, behave and evolve.

#### Active Galactic Nuclei

Skills: 4

[activeGalacticNuclei.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/activeGalacticNuclei/activeGalacticNuclei.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** In some galaxies, accretion onto a central supermassive black hole generates radiation and outflows that differ from normal starlight.

**User-friendly description (en):** Investigate galaxy centres where material falling toward black holes generates immense energy.

##### Accretion-Powered Emission

[accretionPoweredEmission.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/activeGalacticNuclei/skills/accretionPoweredEmission.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how infalling material can release substantial radiation before crossing an event horizon.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how material falling toward a black hole can produce powerful radiation.

##### Quasars

[quasars.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/activeGalacticNuclei/skills/quasars.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify quasars as luminous manifestations of active galactic nuclei, including the implications of their cosmological distances.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize quasars as extremely bright examples of active galactic nuclei.

##### Relativistic Jets

[relativisticJets.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/activeGalacticNuclei/skills/relativisticJets.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the observed collimated outflows in some active galaxies and the role of viewing geometry.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the narrow, fast-moving jets produced by some active galaxies.

##### Supermassive Black Holes

[supermassiveBlackHoles.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/activeGalacticNuclei/skills/supermassiveBlackHoles.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret evidence for compact massive objects in galaxy centers and their influence on nearby orbits.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore the evidence for massive black holes at the centres of galaxies.

#### Galaxies and Their Evolution

Skills: 4

[galaxiesAndTheirEvolution.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/galaxiesAndTheirEvolution/galaxiesAndTheirEvolution.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Galaxies differ in morphology, stellar content, formation history and interaction, rather than representing fixed shapes throughout cosmic time.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore different galaxy shapes and how galaxies change over time.

##### Galaxy Groups and Clusters

[galaxyGroupsAndClusters.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/galaxiesAndTheirEvolution/skills/galaxyGroupsAndClusters.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret gravitationally associated galaxy populations and their larger-scale environments.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how gravity gathers galaxies into groups and clusters.

##### Galaxy Interactions and Mergers

[galaxyInteractionsAndMergers.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/galaxiesAndTheirEvolution/skills/galaxyInteractionsAndMergers.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how gravitational encounters alter galaxy structures, gas and star formation.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how encounters and mergers can reshape galaxies and trigger new stars.

##### Galaxy Morphology

[galaxyMorphology.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/galaxiesAndTheirEvolution/skills/galaxyMorphology.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish spiral, elliptical and irregular galaxies while recognizing that visual shape alone does not determine history.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize spiral, elliptical and irregular galaxies without treating shape as their full history.

##### Galaxy Stellar Populations

[galaxyStellarPopulations.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/galaxiesAndTheirEvolution/skills/galaxyStellarPopulations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Infer differences in star formation and past evolution from stellar colors, spectra and age indicators.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use a galaxy's light to infer differences in its stars and star-formation history.

#### Interstellar Matter

Skills: 4

[interstellarMatter.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/interstellarMatter/interstellarMatter.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Gas, dust, radiation and magnetic fields between stars are active participants in the cycling of matter across galaxies.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how gas, dust and magnetic fields influence the space between stars.

##### Interstellar Chemical Cycling

[interstellarChemicalCycling.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/interstellarMatter/skills/interstellarChemicalCycling.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how stellar outflows and explosive events replenish and alter material available for new star formation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how dying stars return material to space for new generations of stars.

##### Interstellar Dust

[interstellarDust.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/interstellarMatter/skills/interstellarDust.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain extinction, reddening and infrared emission caused by dust along astronomical sightlines.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how interstellar dust dims, reddens and re-emits starlight.

##### Interstellar Gas

[interstellarGas.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/interstellarMatter/skills/interstellarGas.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret evidence for diffuse ionized, neutral and molecular gas and the conditions associated with these phases.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish different forms of gas found between stars.

##### Nebulae

[nebulae.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/interstellarMatter/skills/nebulae.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish emission, reflection and dark nebulae by their observable mechanisms and relation to surrounding light sources.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize different kinds of nebulae by the way they interact with light.

#### The Milky Way

Skills: 4

[theMilkyWay.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/theMilkyWay/theMilkyWay.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Our galaxy is mapped from an interior viewpoint by combining stellar distributions, gas, motions and distance measurements.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how astronomers map the Milky Way from inside it.

##### Galactic Rotation

[galacticRotation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/theMilkyWay/skills/galacticRotation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how orbital motions and measured velocities reveal the distribution of mass in the Milky Way.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use the motion of stars and gas to learn how mass is distributed in our galaxy.

##### Milky Way Structure

[milkyWayStructure.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/theMilkyWay/skills/milkyWayStructure.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret the disk, spiral structure, bulge and halo and explain how they are inferred from our position within the galaxy.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify the disk, central bulge and halo of our galaxy.

##### Solar System's Galactic Location

[solarSystemsGalacticLocation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/theMilkyWay/skills/solarSystemsGalacticLocation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Locate the Sun approximately within the Galactic disk, distinguishing its local spiral-arm environment from the Galactic center.

**User-friendly description (en):** Locate the Solar System within the Milky Way rather than at its centre.

##### Star Clusters

[starClusters.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/interstellarAndGalacticAstronomy/theMilkyWay/skills/starClusters.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish open and globular clusters by structure, typical populations and galactic environments.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare open and globular star clusters and where they are found.

### Observing the Sky

Groups: 4 · Skills: 19

[observingTheSky.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/observingTheSky.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** This domain addresses how celestial positions, patterns, brightness and changes are represented from an observer's location on Earth. It treats the sky as an observable system while distinguishing apparent motion from the physical causes developed in celestial mechanics.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to describe where objects appear in the sky and how their positions change with time and location.

#### Astronomical Time

Skills: 5

[astronomicalTime.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/astronomicalTime/astronomicalTime.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Timekeeping conventions derived from repeated celestial cycles support observation and comparison across dates, without constituting a curriculum in civil time zones.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how recurring movements of the Sun, Moon and stars are used to measure time.

##### Astronomical Dates and Epochs

[astronomicalDatesAndEpochs.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/astronomicalTime/skills/astronomicalDatesAndEpochs.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret a standard astronomical date or reference epoch when comparing observations made at different times.

**User-friendly description (en):** Interpret astronomical dates and reference epochs when comparing observations.

##### Lunar Calendar Cycles

[lunarCalendarCycles.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/astronomicalTime/skills/lunarCalendarCycles.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate lunar-based calendar intervals to Moon phases while recognizing different calendar conventions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect the changing phases of the Moon with lunar calendar cycles.

##### Sidereal Time

[siderealTime.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/astronomicalTime/skills/siderealTime.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how rotation relative to distant stars defines sidereal time and predicts which celestial coordinates cross a local meridian.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use the stars' apparent motion to understand sidereal time.

##### Solar Calendar Cycles

[solarCalendarCycles.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/astronomicalTime/skills/solarCalendarCycles.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate solar-year calendar intervals to Earth's annual revolution and seasons without assuming universal calendar rules.

**User-friendly description (en):** Connect the annual motion of Earth with solar calendar cycles.

##### Solar Time

[solarTime.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/astronomicalTime/skills/solarTime.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe Sun-referenced time as related to the apparent position of the Sun, including mean and apparent solar conventions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how the Sun's position relates to solar time.

#### Observation Practice

Skills: 4

[observationPractice.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/observationPractice/observationPractice.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Reliable sky observation requires choosing conditions, finding objects, maintaining records and avoiding preventable observational hazards.

**User-friendly description (en):** Plan safe, useful sky observations and keep records that others can understand.

##### Astronomical Observation Records

[astronomicalObservationRecords.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/observationPractice/skills/astronomicalObservationRecords.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Record the time, location, conditions, method and observed changes so that a sighting can be interpreted or compared.

**User-friendly description (en):** Record when, where and how you saw something in the sky.

##### Observing Conditions

[observingConditions.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/observationPractice/skills/observingConditions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate how clouds, atmospheric turbulence, transparency, artificial light and horizon obstructions affect a planned observation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Choose observing times and places with suitable weather, darkness and visibility.

##### Safe Solar Observation

[safeSolarObservation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/observationPractice/skills/safeSolarObservation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish approved solar-viewing methods from unsafe direct viewing or unfiltered optical magnification.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify safe ways to view the Sun and avoid methods that can damage eyesight.

##### Sky Maps and Star Charts

[skyMapsAndStarCharts.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/observationPractice/skills/skyMapsAndStarCharts.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use a chart or planetarium representation to identify celestial directions, objects and visibility for a specified place and time.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read a sky map for a particular location and date.

#### Sky Geometry

Skills: 4

[skyGeometry.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyGeometry/skyGeometry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Positions and separations in the visible sky can be communicated through directional frames and angular quantities rather than terrestrial distance alone.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use angles and sky coordinates to describe the direction of objects seen from Earth.

##### Angular Separation

[angularSeparation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyGeometry/skills/angularSeparation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine or compare angular distances and apparent sizes on the sky independently of an object's physical diameter or distance.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare how far apart objects appear in the sky using angles rather than kilometres.

##### Celestial Sphere

[celestialSphere.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyGeometry/skills/celestialSphere.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret the apparent projection of distant objects onto an imaginary sphere without treating that sphere as a physical shell.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand the imaginary celestial sphere used to map the night sky.

##### Equatorial Coordinates

[equatorialCoordinates.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyGeometry/skills/equatorialCoordinates.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret right ascension and declination as a coordinate system tied to Earth's rotational axis.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read right ascension and declination to locate objects on a celestial map.

##### Horizon Coordinates

[horizonCoordinates.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyGeometry/skills/horizonCoordinates.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Locate a celestial object using altitude and azimuth relative to an observer's horizon and orientation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Find a sky object's direction using its height above the horizon and compass bearing.

#### Sky Patterns

Skills: 6

[skyPatterns.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyPatterns/skyPatterns.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognizable configurations make celestial scenes navigable, but their visibility and apparent arrangement depend on viewpoint and date.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize sky patterns and understand how their visibility changes.

##### Apparent Brightness

[apparentBrightness.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyPatterns/skills/apparentBrightness.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare how bright celestial objects look from Earth without equating observed brightness with intrinsic luminosity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare how bright objects look from Earth, without confusing brightness with their actual light output.

##### Asterisms

[asterisms.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyPatterns/skills/asterisms.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize named visual star patterns that can cross constellation boundaries and distinguish them from officially defined regions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify familiar star patterns that are not necessarily official constellations.

##### Constellations

[constellations.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyPatterns/skills/constellations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use officially defined regions of the celestial sphere to locate objects without assuming their member stars form a physical cluster.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use constellation regions to locate objects without assuming their stars are physically close together.

##### Daily Sky Motion

[dailySkyMotion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyPatterns/skills/dailySkyMotion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe the apparent east-to-west paths of celestial objects across the sky, including circumpolar paths.

**User-friendly description (en):** Describe how stars appear to travel across the sky during a day or night.

##### Seasonal Sky Visibility

[seasonalSkyVisibility.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyPatterns/skills/seasonalSkyVisibility.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why different stars and constellations become visible at different times of the year.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why different star patterns are visible in different seasons.

##### Stellar Proper Motion

[stellarProperMotion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/observingTheSky/skyPatterns/skills/stellarProperMotion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify the slow positional motion of a star relative to distant background sources and distinguish this physical change from the daily apparent rotation of the sky.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize a star's very slow movement against more distant stars.

### Planetary Science

Groups: 4 · Skills: 18

[planetaryScience.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/planetaryScience.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Planetary science compares worlds by their surfaces, interiors, atmospheres and volatile materials. It uses Earth as one comparative case, but its categories also apply to moons, dwarf planets and worlds beyond the Solar System.

**User-friendly description (en):** Investigate what worlds are made of and how their surfaces, atmospheres and interiors work.

#### Atmospheres and Weather

Skills: 4

[atmospheresAndWeather.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/atmospheresAndWeather/atmospheresAndWeather.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Atmospheric behavior depends on composition, gravity, radiation, pressure and circulation in ways that vary widely from Earth.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover why different planets have very different weather and atmospheres.

##### Atmospheric Circulation

[atmosphericCirculation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/atmospheresAndWeather/skills/atmosphericCirculation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate global winds and thermal patterns to solar input, rotation and atmospheric structure.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how a planet's rotation and heating shape large-scale air movement.

##### Atmospheric Retention and Escape

[atmosphericRetentionAndEscape.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/atmospheresAndWeather/skills/atmosphericRetentionAndEscape.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how gravity, temperature and escape processes influence the presence or loss of planetary atmospheres.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why some worlds keep thick atmospheres while others lose gas to space.

##### Planetary Greenhouse Effects

[planetaryGreenhouseEffects.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/atmospheresAndWeather/skills/planetaryGreenhouseEffects.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how atmospheric absorption and emission influence surface or atmospheric temperatures on different worlds.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how atmospheric gases trap and release heat on different planets.

##### Planetary Weather

[planetaryWeather.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/atmospheresAndWeather/skills/planetaryWeather.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify and interpret weather phenomena such as storms, clouds and winds under non-Earth conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize storms, winds and clouds on worlds with conditions unlike Earth's.

#### Interiors and Volatiles

Skills: 5

[interiorsAndVolatiles.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/interiorsAndVolatiles/interiorsAndVolatiles.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Indirect observations of magnetic fields, heat and fluid materials constrain unseen layers and possible activity beneath planetary surfaces.

**User-friendly description (en):** Investigate hidden planetary layers, magnetic fields, water and ice.

##### Cryovolcanism

[cryovolcanism.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/interiorsAndVolatiles/skills/cryovolcanism.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Recognize and explain eruptions driven by volatile liquids and ices rather than molten rock.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how cold worlds can erupt icy or volatile materials instead of molten rock.

##### Planetary Interior Structure

[planetaryInteriorStructure.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/interiorsAndVolatiles/skills/planetaryInteriorStructure.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Infer cores, mantles or other layers from density, seismic, magnetic and gravitational evidence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use indirect evidence to explore a planet's core and interior layers.

##### Planetary Magnetic Fields

[planetaryMagneticFields.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/interiorsAndVolatiles/skills/planetaryMagneticFields.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the conditions under which internal conductive flows can generate global or regional magnetic fields.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how moving conductive material inside a planet can create a magnetic field.

##### Subsurface Oceans

[subsurfaceOceans.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/interiorsAndVolatiles/skills/subsurfaceOceans.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret geophysical and compositional evidence for liquids beneath icy surfaces without assuming biology.

**User-friendly description (en):** Investigate the clues that some icy moons may hide liquid oceans.

##### Water and Ice Beyond Earth

[waterAndIceBeyondEarth.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/interiorsAndVolatiles/skills/waterAndIceBeyondEarth.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate the physical states and likely reservoirs of water on different Solar System bodies.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore where water and ice may exist on other worlds.

#### Planetary Classes

Skills: 5

[planetaryClasses.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/planetaryClasses/planetaryClasses.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Composition, density and thermal history help explain why planets and moons display very different structures rather than simply different sizes.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare rocky worlds, giant planets, moons and other planetary bodies.

##### Giant Planets

[giantPlanets.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/planetaryClasses/skills/giantPlanets.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish gas giants from ice giants using composition, interior models and observable atmospheric properties.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish gas giants and ice giants by their composition and internal structure.

##### Natural Satellites

[naturalSatellites.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/planetaryClasses/skills/naturalSatellites.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare moons by origin, orbit, composition and geological activity without treating all satellites as Moon-like.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how moons differ in size, origin, composition and activity.

##### Planetary Density and Composition

[planetaryDensityAndComposition.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/planetaryClasses/skills/planetaryDensityAndComposition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use mass, radius and density to constrain plausible bulk material and planetary classification.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use a world's mass, size and density to reason about what it contains.

##### Planetary Ring Systems

[planetaryRingSystems.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/planetaryClasses/skills/planetaryRingSystems.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret the composition, dynamics, formation and evolution of rings around planets or other bodies, including interactions with nearby satellites and differences between dense rings and diffuse dust populations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how planetary rings form, change and interact with nearby moons.

##### Terrestrial Planets

[terrestrialPlanets.data.ts](../../../learningApps/astronomy/data/skills/planetaryScience/planetaryClasses/skills/terrestrialPlanets.data.ts)
